    CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS

  POLICY AND MANAGEMENT

  MEMORANDUM

 TO:  City Council Liaison / Chamber of Commerce Committee
 FROM:  Chad Lynn, Deputy Director of Special Projects, Public Safety

 DATE:  October 30, 2025

 SUBJECT:  Update on Fiscal Year 2025-2026 Quarters One Programs and Initiatives
  for the Beverly Hills Chamber of Commerce

 ATTACHMENT:  1. Chamber of Commerce 2024-2025 Work Plan Summary
  2. Chamber of Commerce Work Plan Tracker (General and Marketing
  by Chamber and vendor PSM)

INTRODUCTION
This item provides the City Council Chamber of Commerce Committee Liaisons Mayor
Nazarian and Councilmember Wells (Liaisons) an update of the programs and initiatives of the
Beverly Hills Chamber of Commerce (Chamber) during quarters one Fiscal Year 2025-2026.
Additionally, he Chamber is requesting repurposing of specific programs for FY 25/26 to more
effectively address anticipated community needs. A review of the progress on approved
workplan programs per quarter is required per the agreement between the Chamber and City.

DISCUSSION
The Beverly Hills Chamber of Commerce is contracted by the City to provide a range of economic
development programs which reflect City priorities, seek to retain existing businesses, and attract
new businesses to Beverly Hills. The Chamber’s focus is on economic development for the
community, fostering business-to-business relationships, and to act as a liaison between the City
and business community. An agreement detailing the workplan between the City and Chamber
was approved for FY 25/26 on July 1, 2025, a summary of which has been provided as
Attachment 1.

The agreement between the City and Chamber includes quarterly updates on the programs and
initiatives. The workplan for FY 25/26 also included the carryover workplan items for FY 24/25
which included one Small Business Task Force Meeting and one Property Owners Task Force
Meeting. These carryovers would be carried out in FY 25/26, in addition to the four required
meetings for the current Fiscal Year.

They Chamber will provide a more detailed update of their workplan items during the presentation
of the meeting. Updates will include:
 • Marketing and outreach support for City and Partner events, functions, and initiatives,
  including the events related to the Mayors initiatives such as Spotlight with Sharona
   o  Two Spotlight with Sharona events were completed during quarter one, which
  included Gravitas & S. Beverly Dr
  ▪ S. Beverly Dr featured Urth Caffe, Le Reve Beauty Lounge, Pompadour
  Beverly Hills & Beverly Hills Cookies
  •  Property Owner’s Task Force (1 of 5 – 1 Carryover from FY 24/25)
  •  Small Business Task Force (1 of 5 – 1 Carryover from FY 24/25)
  •  Mayoral Business Retention Meetings (3 of 12)
  •  New Businesses Newsletter (1 of 4, with 1 scheduled for release in Q2)
  •  Social Media Campaigns (Sip and Savor) and Newsletter for NOW Beverly Hills shop local
  program with vendor PSM
  •  Metro Subway Stakeholder Meetings (3 of 12 – Nov and Dec Cancelled w/Metro)
  •  New York Business Attraction and Retention Mission Planning and Scheduling

Additionally, the Chamber hosted 8 ribbon cuttings for businesses during quarter one with the
special event permit fees waived, per the approved workplan. On September 25th, the Chamber
hosted An Evening with the Mayor at Greystone Mansion. A full tracker for the items can be found
in Attachment 2.

Based on the completed tasks, the Chamber is generally on target for their workplan at the close
of the first quarter. Scheduling challenges for task force work, along with delayed work related to
Metro functions are anticipated to create challenges to meeting workplan goals in upcoming
quarters for the following:
  • Property Owner’s Task Force, including additional carryover meetings from 24/25
  • Small Business Task Force, including additional carryover meetings from 24/25
  • Metro Subway Stakeholder Meetings

In order to more evenly spread out work throughout the year, and to avoid clustering task force
meetings in the latter quarters of the fiscal year, the Chamber is proposing repurposing hours
associated with these workplan items. Proposals for use of this time including the following:
  • Education for the City’s Green Building Initiative in partnership with Public Works and
  Environmental Innovation
  • Reintroduction of Small Business Development Center
  • Metro Focus Group Discussion(s) for La Cienga Station Opening
  • Other programs for consideration

The New York Business Attraction and Retention mission was conducted October 20th through
October 24th. Although this work was completed during the second quarter of the fiscal year, a
brief update will be provided at this meeting.

FISCAL IMPACT
There is no fiscal impact from reviewing this item as the funding was already accounted for in the
FY 25/26 Chamber contract in the total not to exceed amount of $553,245. Funding for the
Chamber’s total contract of $553,245 is funded through the Policy & Management Department’s
Business Development budget in the amount of $380,000, with the remaining $173,245 funded
from the Tourism and Marketing budget for Chamber initiatives which are tourism and marketing

  2 of 2
 focused. Metro related workplan expenses related to the Metro Purple Line Extension and are
reimbursable by Metro, and staff will continue to work with the Chamber to ensure reimbursement
for these expenses.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends the Liaison Committee review and provide recommendations for the Chamber
of Commerce quarters two and three program and initiative updates for FY 24/25.
